ga.text: General and Administrative Expense. General and administrative expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $4.0 million and $2.5 million, respectively. The Company’s general and administrative expense primarily relates to professional fees, regulatory fees, marketing and investor relations, payroll and stock-based compensation expense. The increase was primarily due to the expanded scale of the Company’s operations, following the acquisition of Dolly Varden, including higher payroll, professional fees and regulatory costs.

intro.text: Contango ORE, Inc. (“CORE” or the “Company”) was formed on September 1, 2010 as a Delaware corporation for the purpose of engaging in the exploration for and development of gold ore and associated minerals in the State of Alaska. On January 8, 2015, CORE Alaska, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (“CORE Alaska”), and a subsidiary of Royal Gold, Inc. (“Royal Gold”) formed Peak Gold, LLC (the “Peak Gold JV”). On September 30, 2020, CORE Alaska sold a 30% membership interest in the Peak Gold JV to KG Mining (Alaska), Inc. (“KG Mining”), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Kinross Gold Corporation (“Kinross”), a large gold producer with a diverse global portfolio and extensive operating experience in Alaska. The sale is referred to herein as the “CORE Transactions”.

s.t: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the unrealized gain on marketable securities totaled $0.5 million and was primarily due to changes in the fair value of the Company's investment in Onyx, compared to an unrealized loss of $1.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the unrealized gain on marketable securities totaled $0.3 million and was primarily due to changes in the fair value of the Company's investment in Onyx, compared to an unrealized gain of $5.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
The income from the Company’s equity investment in the Peak Gold JV for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $6.9 million compared to income of $29.5 million for the same period in 2025.
The income from the Company’s equity investment in the Peak Gold JV for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $28.9 million compared to income of $79.2 million for the same period in 2025.

The difference between the carrying value of the Company's investment in the Peak Gold JV and its proportionate share of the Peak Gold JV's members' equity is primarily attributable to previously suspended equity-method losses that were recognized based on historical ownership percentages.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company decreased its cash balance primarily through cash used in operating and investing activities, partially offset by financing activities, the acquisition of Dolly Varden and distributions from the Peak Gold JV.

Based on its current working capital, anticipated operating and investing activities, expected distributions from the Peak Gold JV, and demonstrated ability to access the equity capital markets, management believes the Company will have sufficient liquidity to meet its anticipated capital and working capital requirements.

As of September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, the Company's cumulative investment in the Peak Gold JV exceeded its cumulative losses, which allowed the Company to recognize its investment of $ 58.0 million and $ 52.7 million, respectively.
The Peak Gold JV funds its operations from cash flows generated from operations, and the Company does not anticipate future cash calls from the joint venture.
The following table is a roll-forward of the Company’s investment in the Peak Gold JV as of September 30, 2026:

In July 2025, the Company filed a motion to intervene as a defendant in the lawsuit to protect its legal rights under the Section 404 permit, its significant investment in the Johnson Tract, and its mineral exploration lease with CIRI.

The CODM uses quarterly financial information (income from equity investment from Peak Gold JV) of the Peak Gold JV in his evaluation of the performance of the Peak Gold JV and can make decisions regarding resource allocations within the Company.

The CODM considers budget to actual and forecast to actual comparison of exploration expenditures and income from equity investment of Peak Gold JV on a quarterly basis when making decisions about the allocation of operating and capital resources to each segment.
The Peak Gold JV is a related party of the Company due to its 30 % equity method investment in it.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company did no t make contributions to the Peak Gold JV but did receive distributions from it (see Note 5 - Investment in the Peak Gold JV).
• Ability to retain or maintain capital contributions to, and our relative ownership interest, in the Peak Gold JV;

The Company’s sources of cash have been from common stock offerings, the issuance of the Debenture, distributions from the equity investment, the proceeds from the Facility (see Note 5 - Investment in the Peak Gold JV, Note 8 - Stockholders' Equity and Note 13 - Debt, for a discussion of the recent activity), and the acquisition of Dolly Varden (see Note 16 - Acquisition).

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
